summary: NUMERIC_CONSTANTS exempts exact bare digit strings with no context check, and several of them (2147483647/2147483648, 2166136261, 2246822507, 3432918353, 3266489909) are valid 10-digit US numbers, so a real phone number equal to one of them is silently not reported even right after 'phone'/'call'.
evidence: Scratch script: scan('phone 2147483648') -> [] and scan('call me 2166136261') -> []; '+2147483647' still reports pii.phone.e164.

summary: The version-shape branch of looksLikeAtFilename treats any domain of two or more all-digit labels plus any TLD as a filename, so real addresses on numeric subdomains like x@1.2.com or jo@1.2.net are dropped from pii.email.
evidence: Scratch script: scan('ping x@1.2.com') -> [] and scan('jo@1.2.net') -> []; regex /^\d+(?:\.\d+)+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$/ accepts '1.2.com'.

summary: looksLikeAtFilename exempts any pii.email span whose domain ends in a non-TLD file extension, even when a real domain comes before the extension. Real addresses inside filenames (e.g. alice.smith@gmail.com.json, bob@corp.com.csv) are no longer reported, which is a regression in the redaction guard.
evidence: On main, scan('key file alice.smith@gmail.com.json'), scan('export bob.jones@acme-corp.com.csv') and scan('bob@acme-corp.com.log') each return ["pii.email"]. On this branch all three return []. So does 'deploy@my-proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com.json'. The guard is `NON_TLD_EXTENSION.test(domain) || ...`, where domain is everything after the last '@' (e.g. 'gmail.com.json'), and it never checks that the part before the extension is a version or single label.
